guarantees.claim: prd_masking is always assigned to prd_i[17:8].
in_mask_basis_x is assigned to aes_mvm(mask_i, A2X) when op_i == CIPH_FWD, aes_mvm(mask_i, S2X) when op_i == CIPH_INV, else aes_mvm(mask_i, A2X).
out_mask_basis_x is assigned to aes_mvm(mask_o, A2X) when op_i == CIPH_INV, aes_mvm(mask_o, S2X) when op_i == CIPH_FWD, else aes_mvm(mask_o, S2X).
Instance u_aes_masked_inverse_gf2p8 connects in_data_basis_x to .a, in_mask_basis_x to .m, out_mask_basis_x to .n, prd_masking to .prd, and drives out_data_basis_x from .a_inv.
data_o is assigned to (aes_mvm(out_data_basis_x, X2S) ^ 8'h63) when op_i == CIPH_FWD, aes_mvm(out_data_basis_x, X2A) when op_i == CIPH_INV, else (aes_mvm(out_data_basis_x, X2S) ^ 8'h63).

assumptions.claim: The op_i input is restricted to the defined operational mode values CIPH_FWD or CIPH_INV; any other value triggers default forward-mode basis conversions which may not match the inversion instance's expected mask basis.
assumptions.cond: when op_i is not CIPH_FWD nor CIPH_INV
assumptions.risk: Mismatched basis conversions can break the masking scheme and leak secret intermediate values.

assumptions.claim: mask_i and mask_o are valid mask values whose basis-converted forms (via A2X or S2X) produce the correct mask inputs for the masked inversion.
assumptions.risk: Invalid mask vectors could corrupt the masked computation, enabling side-channel leakage.

assumptions.claim: prd_i provides random fresh bits for prd_masking; prd_i[17:8] must be unpredictable and not reused across gadgets.
assumptions.risk: Predictable or reused prd values can break the inter-gadget non-interference property of the masking scheme, exposing secrets.

assumptions.claim: The aes_mvm function correctly computes matrix-vector multiplication for the given constant matrices A2X, S2X, X2S, X2A.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect basis transformations would invalidate all masking protections.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case for op_i in all muxes corresponds to forward-mode basis conversions, but it is unclear whether op_i can legally assume other values (e.g., key schedule mode) that would require different conversions. If such a mode exists, the S-box output would be incorrect and potentially leak secrets.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect data_o due to wrong basis conversion and/or missing/wrong affine constant, breaking masked output and potentially exposing secret state.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment states that the addition of constant 8'h63 is skipped for mask conversions, but it is added for data_o in forward mode. It is uncertain if this matches the required algebraic masking relationships for all operating modes, especially when op_i changes dynamically.
uncertain_points.cond: when transitioning between modes or during startup
uncertain_points.risk: If the mask and data paths are not perfectly aligned, the masking scheme may introduce bias or leak secrets during operations.

uncertain_points.claim: The prd_masking slice (prd_i[17:8]) may be shared with other masked gadgets outside this module, increasing the risk of entropy reuse that could compromise non-interference.
uncertain_points.cond: if prd_i bits are also used elsewhere
uncertain_points.risk: Entropy reuse across gadgets can lead to biased joint distributions, enabling higher-order DPA attacks.
